summary.intent: Continue improving quality and performance of the caliper project: correct stale performance claims in docs, add typed checker request structs, and evaluate the redesigned #518 (fewer filesystem calls) PR.
summary.outcome: Pushed a docs branch recording measured checker-on performance (2–9× cold, 6–30× warm) and started a typed-request worker. The redesigned #518 was reviewed and found to yield no wall-time gain, so the assistant recommended closing its memo change and splitting out the differential test.

repo: docs/performance.md still quoted old 15–39× figures from the structural resolver; the new section records checker-on numbers measured on real corpora.
Docs must follow a banned-words list, and the lint gate is `just lint doc-check machete typos`.
oxc's tsconfig cache is order-sensitive: results depend on which consumer touches a config first. Base's own tsconfig validation deliberately primes the context's cache.
Sharing an oxc resolver cache (including between `main` and `types_first`) caused failures (14 in the model test); moving the tsconfig check to a throwaway resolver caused 4 failures.
The larger filesystem cost lies in tsrs (`realpath`, `read_file`, `exists`), not in the Loader memos.
Timeout-as-watchdog work overlaps `rpc.rs` with the typed-request work, so it must wait for that to land.

code.finding: Loader memos were rewritten as loops with one-time per-directory probes, removing recursion deadlock risk; the redesign yields only 1–11% fewer FS calls and no wall/CPU gain.
New model-based differential test (64 tsconfig layouts × 6 orders × both resolvers) catches the cache-sharing findings under mutation; worth keeping independently.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user approval; the assistant verified the diffstat, PR body and evidence before judging the work.
Worktrees were used to isolate doc changes (perf-record) from in-flight PR work.
Findings on the review platform (Entire) were resolved by citing the commit and test that fix them.
Check performance claims against measured data; three table cells were corrected to match the runs.

friction: Benchmark load was 17–28, making wall-time comparisons noisy and unreliable.
The first attempt to resolve an Entire finding had already gone through, causing a duplicate action.
The #518 worker did not run gate_harness or /code-review on the final head, and finding 1 was not re-proved on it.
Moving the tsconfig check to a throwaway resolver, as briefed, broke tests, forcing a different design.
open_items: Decision pending: whether to have a worker split the test-only differential test out of #518 into a small PR; #518 stays as is until then.
Typed checker request structs worker (trail 470) is still running.
Docs PR for the performance record (branch docs/perf-record-2026-11-23, trail 471) awaits opening and review.
#519 (readonly from flags) is ready after review fixes and awaits user action.
Timeout as a loud watchdog is deferred until the typed-request work lands.
A quiet-machine A/B of early-session reuse (#515) needs an idle machine.
Running the weekly oracle on the merged batch is the user's call because of cost.
The MUI extraction gap investigation is blocked on knowing where a MUI corpus lives.
tsrs filesystem cost (`realpath`, `read_file`, `exists`) should be taken up in the other tsrs sessions.
